choragwie: Long ago... this land was divided among seven kingdoms, and each of them wanted all of it.
handan: In one of them, in the city of Hahn-dahn, a boy named Jung was born, the son of a Chin prince, handed to the enemy as a hostage.
oblezenie: Chin was besieging that very city, so the neighbors had every reason to hate a boy from the enemy's family.
kupiec: But the father caught the eye of a rich merchant, Lew Boo-way, [chuckle] who decided that a prince in exile was an investment that could earn him a kingdom.
ucieczka: The merchant bribed the guards and smuggled the prince back to Chin... while the boy was left in Hahn-dahn, among enemies.
powrot: He was nine when he was finally allowed to leave, [sigh] for a country he had never seen.
krol13: Three years later his father was dead, and thirteen-year-old Jung became King of Chin.
regent: The merchant, now Chancellor Lew Boo-way, ruled in his place. And the boy on the throne learned to watch... and keep silent.
nauka: He also learned what his teachers preached: that people obey only reward, and punishment.
dorosl: When he came of age, a revolt broke out at court, because his mother's lover wanted to put his own sons on the throne.
odprawa: [dramatic] Jung crushed the revolt within days, and dismissed the chancellor who had brought the conspirator to court.
trucizna: Lew Boo-way drank poison... before he reached his place of exile.
lisi: From then on, the king answered to no one. And the man closest to him was a new adviser, Lee Suh.
mapa: Lee Suh kept telling him that the six kingdoms had to be swallowed now, while they were divided and weak.
machina: Chin was ready. Because for a hundred years every peasant here had been a soldier, and promotion was earned with the heads of slain enemies.
kusze: His crossbowmen fired weapons built from identical parts, that fit any crossbow.
kanal: Even an enemy helped him. [chuckle] An engineer sent to ruin Chin with a giant construction project dug a canal that ended up feeding its army.
wymarsz: [dramatic] In two hundred and thirty B.C., the army of Chin marched east, and began with its weakest neighbor.
zhao: Two years later Jow fell, and the king returned to Hahn-dahn, to settle scores with those who had tormented his family.
poselstwo: The neighbors now knew what was coming. So the Crown Prince of Yen sent a man to Chin... to kill the king.
dary: Jing Kuh brought two gifts: the head of a fugitive general, and a map of the lands Yen was supposedly surrendering.
sztylet: [whispering] Hidden inside the rolled-up map... was a dagger.
kolumna: [gasp] The king ran around a pillar! Because his sword was so long that he couldn't draw it from its scabbard. [chuckle]
lekarz: Courtiers were forbidden to carry weapons, so a physician hurled his bag of medicines at the assassin.
pretekst: Jing Kuh died at the foot of the pillar, and the king got the pretext he needed for war with Yen.
ksiaze: The prince who had sent the assassin was put to death on his own father's orders... but that did not save Yen.
wei: The capital of Way had walls that could not be taken. So a general turned a river against it, and after three months, [sigh] the walls simply gave way.
chu: Against mighty Choo, the king sent six hundred thousand men... nearly everything he had.
qi: The last kingdom surrendered without a fight, in two hundred and twenty-one B.C.
mapa2: In nine years, the black of Chin covered the entire map.
czarne: [dramatic] For the first time, the whole country had a single ruler.
cesarz: The title of king seemed too small to him. [chuckle] So he invented a new one: First Emperor.
posagi: He had the weapons of the defeated melted down into twelve colossal bronze statues.
drogi: He linked the country with roads, on which every cart ran on axles of the same width.
prowincje: He divided the land into thirty-six provinces, and sent officials there whom he could recall at any moment.
rody: He ordered the old noble clans to abandon their castles. And a hundred and twenty thousand families moved to the capital... under his eye.
stela: He toured the country, and on sacred mountains he had it carved in stone, that he had brought peace to the world.
kanal2: In the south, his engineers joined two rivers with a canal, so the army could sail even farther.
pismo: He also made everyone write with the same characters, so his orders would be understood in every province.
moneta: From then on, the same coin was used everywhere.
miara: Weights and measures were to be the same everywhere, too.
mur: In the north, he ordered the old walls joined into one, to stop the horsemen of the steppe.
robotnicy: It was built by hundreds of thousands of soldiers, convicts and peasants. [sigh] And many of them stayed beneath the wall forever.
ksiegi: When scholars began praising the old days... he had their books burned.
uczeni: A year later he had several hundred scholars executed. And when his own son Foo-soo spoke up for them, he sent him north, to the Wall.
zmierzch: [sigh] Only one enemy was left that he could not defeat... his own death.
mlot: On one of his journeys, [gasp] an iron hammer smashed the carriage right next to his own.
morze: So he sent ships to the Eastern Sea, having heard that immortals lived on the islands there.
xufu: The magician Shoo Foo sailed there with thousands of boys and girls... and never came back.
rtec: He is also said to have swallowed mercury pills meant to prolong his life, [chuckle] which most likely shortened it.
przejscia: [whispering] The emperor now hid in palaces linked by covered walkways, so that no one would know where he slept.
meteor: When a meteorite fell, someone carved on it that the First Emperor would die, and his land would be divided.
palac: He also began building a palace so vast, that a single hall was meant to hold ten thousand people.
kopiec: And from the first year of his reign, seven hundred thousand people dug his tomb beneath Mount Lee.
armia: He had thousands of life-size soldiers made of clay... to guard him even after death.
rzeki: According to the chronicles, rivers of mercury flowed through the tomb, and crossbows were set to fire at anyone who entered.
podroz: In two hundred and ten B.C., he set out on another tour of the country, and fell ill on the road.
koniec: [sigh] He died in the summer, far from the capital, at the age of forty-nine.
spisek: [whispering] Chancellor Lee Suh and the eunuch Jow Gow concealed his death, because they wanted to choose the successor themselves.
ryby: The carriage rolled on, as if nothing had happened. And to keep the heat from giving away the truth... [sigh] carts of salted fish were placed beside it.
list: The eldest son received a forged letter, in which his father ordered him to take his own life... and he obeyed.
huhai: The throne went to a younger son, Hoo-hi, who listened to the eunuch in everything.
powstanie: Just a year later, peasants driven to serve on the frontier rose in revolt, and the whole country followed them.
upadek: The dynasty that was meant to last ten thousand generations... [chuckle] fell after fifteen years.
studnia: The clay army was found only in nineteen seventy-four, by farmers digging a well.
grobowiec: [whispering] To this day, no one has opened the tomb itself.
qin: What he left behind is the name we still use for this country. Because China most likely comes from the old Chin.
